name: ml-experiment-rigor
description: Use when building, comparing or reviewing a classic ML or deep learning result. Enforces leakage checks, baselines, uncertainty intervals and a script-computed confidence level.
title: ML and DL experiment rigor
goal: A modelling claim is accepted only with a correct split, a baseline, an uncertainty estimate and evidence. Confidence is computed by a script.
steps: Read `{{skill_dir}}/references/ml-checklist.md` and fill the applicable items with evidence from code, logs and run outputs.
Check the split and every fit step in the code first (items M2, M3, M9). Leakage invalidates everything after it.

Compute or request metrics with an interval: `python3 {{skill_dir}}/scripts/score_decision.py wilson K N` for proportions; a bootstrap (at least 1000 resamples) or repeated seeds for other metrics. State what was done.
Compare against the baseline using a paired method on the same cases. Say 'no demonstrated difference' when intervals overlap.
Write the checklist JSON (`score_decision.py example` shows the shape), run `score_decision.py score FILE.json`, and report its confidence word and numbers unchanged.
List what to run next to close each open item (more seeds, a different split, a slice analysis).
output: Question, data and split summary, baseline and model results with intervals, the script output, open items, and next experiments in priority order.
gotchas: The test set is used once. If it was used to choose anything, say the estimate is optimistic.
If many variants were tried, say how many; the best one is biased upward.
Accuracy on imbalanced data is not evidence.
